1.explanation:
• resources/filters/quarto-pre/code-annotation.lua: This Lua filter is responsible for scanning code blocks in the Pandoc pipeline, extracting trailing comment markers (e.g. “-- <1>” or “// <2>”) and replacing them with circled numbers inline. The fact that VHDL (“vhdl”) and C++ (“cpp”/“c++”) blocks still dump raw comments indicates that the language‐recognition (or comment‐regex) in this filter needs to be extended to handle those languages’ comment syntax.

• src/execute/ojs/annotate-source.ts: When Quarto renders code blocks using the OJS (Quarto’s native HTML) engine, this TypeScript module re-implements much of the same annotation extraction logic on the client side. It currently handles languages like JavaScript/TypeScript/R/Python but doesn’t detect VHDL or C++ comment-styles there. Both server-side (Lua) and client-side (TS) routines must be updated so that “-- <n>” and “// <n>” in vhdl/cpp blocks produce the same circled labels as R and Python.
1.bug_scenario: When you author code‐annotation blocks for VHDL or C/C++ in a .qmd and render to HTML, Quarto still recognizes the “-- <1>” or “// <1>” markers but never replaces them with circled labels inline. Instead you just get the comment blocks collected underneath the code, without any inline “①” in the code. The exact same syntax works correctly for R, Python, TypeScript, etc., so the problem must lie in the code‐annotation logic’s support for C++/VHDL languages.

2.explanation: All of the code-annotation work happens in a Lua filter (code-annotation.lua) that scans code fences for comment markers and emits special Pandoc nodes, and in the custom-nodes definition (decoratedcodeblock.lua) which knows how to collect and render those annotation nodes under the block. Once the Lua side has labelled the annotated code, the TypeScript file annotate-source.ts (used during OJS execution) strips the markers and wires in the HTML wrappers (data-target-annotation attributes, circled numbers, etc.). Currently the Lua filter only recognizes certain languages/comment styles (R, Python, etc.) and never kicks in for C++ (“//”) or VHDL (“--”) blocks. To fix this bug you must update code-annotation.lua to recognize those comment prefixes (and possibly extend decoratedcodeblock.lua if it hard-codes allowed languages), and ensure annotate-source.ts handles the extra fence languages so that the annotation circles and list HTML are injected correctly.
2.bug_scenario: When you render a .qmd document with “code-annotations: below” (or hover/select) you expect every code block comment of the form “// <1>” or “-- <2>” to be turned into numbered circles and linked into an annotation list under the block. In the two screenshots you can see that R and Python chunks get their annotations replaced with circled numbers and lists correctly, but C++, VHDL (and any chunk using “// <n>” or “-- <n>”) still leave the raw “// <1>” or “-- <2>” inline and do not generate the annotation list at all.
